headline: Profit swings positive as fee income grows, deal costs fade
summary_short: Hyatt's Q2 2026 net income swung to $110M from a $3M loss a year ago as 2025's Playa Hotels deal costs rolled off; revenue rose 1.2% y/y to $1,829M as comparable system-wide RevPAR gained 5.9%, even as owned & leased and distribution segment Adjusted EBITDA both declined.
summary_long: Net income attributable to Hyatt rose to $110M (EPS $1.17) from a $3M loss in Q2 2025, mainly because 2025's Playa Hotels Acquisition transaction and integration costs did not repeat, plus higher other income and net fee revenues; the effective tax rate fell to 37.2% from 78.1% on higher pretax income. Revenue grew 1.2% y/y to $1,829M as comparable RevPAR rose 5.9% on leisure/group strength, while distribution revenue fell $37M on weaker Mexico/Jamaica demand. Management & franchising segment Adjusted EBITDA grew 11.6% to $266M; owned & leased and distribution segment Adjusted EBITDA both declined on the Playa Hotels Portfolio sale and lower bookings. Cash plus short-term investments was $606M; Hyatt repurchased $12M and paid $0.15/share in dividends.

drivers.explanation: Net income swung to a $110M profit from a $3M loss a year earlier, driven mainly by an ~$81M drop in transaction and integration costs tied to the 2025 Playa Hotels Acquisition, plus higher net fee revenues and other income.

Gross fee revenues and reimbursed-cost revenues rose on stronger RevPAR (comparable system-wide RevPAR +5.9% y/y) and portfolio growth, while owned & leased and distribution revenue fell on the Playa Hotels Portfolio sale and weaker Mexico/Jamaica bookings.

$113M y/y increase driven by lower transaction/integration costs (no repeat of 2025's Playa Hotels Acquisition costs), higher other income, and higher net fee revenues; effective tax rate fell to 37.2% from 78.1% as pretax income rose.
Tracks the net-income swing to profit; per-share basis also benefited from Q2 2026 share repurchases of $12M trimming the diluted share count versus Q1.

Management & franchising segment Adjusted EBITDA grew 11.6% to $266M on higher gross fee revenues; owned & leased ($40M vs $47M) and distribution ($27M vs $43M) segment Adjusted EBITDA both declined, partly offsetting the gain.

Cash fell versus Q1 and a year ago mainly on $147M of year-to-date share repurchases and $28M of dividends paid, partially offset by operating cash flow; total liquidity including short-term investments and revolver availability was $2,103M.
Down y/y (-$255M) on cumulative share repurchases and dividends paid since Q2 2025, partly offset by retained profit; up q/q (+$78M) as Q2 net income exceeded the quarter's buybacks and dividends.
